description: The largest envelope the structural contract admits, stated as a recipe rather than as two megabytes of committed filler. Step 1.1 owns one question about it: do D3's record maxima actually fit inside D3's 2 MiB input cap, and does native Test-Json accept the result. Step 1.2 owns the rest — that Publish can canonicalize, render and publish this envelope inside its time and memory budget, measured in a child process on every supported CI leg.

ownedByStep.1.1: structural admission and the byte arithmetic below
ownedByStep.1.2: publication runtime, memory growth and the rendered view budgets

generation.filler: New-Filler repeats '<seed>-' until it reaches the requested length, then truncates to it. The alphabet is ASCII letters, digits and hyphen only, so no JSON escape sequence can change the byte count and the character count equals the UTF-8 byte count.
generation.grouping: `rootCause` and `component` are seeded from the group index rather than the finding index, so the 256 raw findings collapse into exactly `mergedGroups` merge keys — the merged maximum the vocabulary declares — while every string still sits at its structural maximum. Eight tasks use maximum diagnostics; each group's two findings use distinct completed-task model labels and title/body/action seeds with at least eight shared tokens, so the maximum fixture enters corroboration candidate processing. Additional diagnostic capacity is reserved for the required scope-authority and model-selection records while the whole fixture stays under the 2 MiB input cap.
